niche: a Norwegian university machine-learning group choosing which shortlisted training configuration to name in a national compute proposal for its seabed sediment classifier, forecasting each one's loss on the mapping programme's verified benchmark from a five-week pilot sweep of real training runs: an expert-label size ladder run at tabled learning rates, a learning-rate check, a few wide runs, and trials of a contractor's labels and of labels transferred from a legacy sediment map that the benchmark never scored
analyst_test: A careful but hurried analyst cleans every export, opens the per-item scores, scores each run on the expert-labelled development items and calibrates that to the benchmark, then fits the field's textbook object, one scaling-law regression over every finished run (a curve in examples, a term in width, each label route's share, a learning-rate term), chooses its form on the largest runs held back, reports the held-back misses although they all fall on one side, and names the configuration trained on every label it can get, at a loss the routes' costs and the bent return do not support.
domain_test: Every result is a scaling-study quantity the field estimates from a sweep of training runs (a score on the target yardstick for runs that yardstick never saw, the loss a noisier label route costs at matched examples and learning rate, the return to more examples past the range run, the learning rate a wider model needs, run-to-run spread, a forecast with a range for configurations larger than any run, chosen because it holds when the largest runs are held out); swap in hospital or retail nouns and learning-rate tuning by width, a development split scored on vendor labels, examples seen and seeds stop making sense.
layer1: trainer logs that repeat step ranges after a preempted job resumes from its last checkpoint
two logger versions with different scalar names and logging cadence
relaunched runs that share a name with a cancelled or failed first launch
benchmark uploads keyed by a truncated checkpoint digest, with repeats and part-way checkpoints
scheduler job attempts, requeues and cancelled jobs for one run
a re-delivered contractor shard whose first receipt stays in the register
an item dump lost to a scratch quota
stakeholder_role: the group lead who signs the compute proposal

spine.entity: one logged training or evaluation scalar of one run
spine.grain: run x logged step x scalar

world.geography: Norway (the northern coast), a national seabed mapping programme with its own compute call
world.org_type: a university machine-learning research group preparing a national compute allocation proposal

driver: A forward level for configurations larger than any yet run is read from a staged pilot in which the return per added unit was measured only on the trusted source, while the configurations to be chosen among add units from cheaper sources whose yield differs: the target yardstick never scored a run that used them, the logged score is taken on a split that includes those sources' own labels and so rewards fitting their errors, their trials ran at other settings than the ladder they are compared with, and the return to more units bends just past the range the trusted source covers, so each source's yield has to be rebuilt on the trusted yardstick at matched settings and carried forward by a form that holds when the largest runs are held out.
driver_concrete: Each shortlisted configuration's loss on the programme's benchmark is forecast from the pilot by scoring every final checkpoint on the expert-labelled development items calibrated to the benchmark's own scores, reading what the contractor's and the map-transfer labels cost against expert-label runs of the same size, width and learning rate, taking the level at each total past the expert pool as its own unknown once those costs are out, carrying it past the largest trial no faster than the last doubling's gain and no slower than none, with the curve checked on the largest runs held back, and stating a range that carries run-to-run spread, the forecast's own error and the yardstick's error.
stump: A careful but hurried analyst fits one scaling curve through every pilot run on the right yardstick, so the curve, which the expert-label ladder dominates, absorbs into the label routes' costs what is a return to more examples that bends just past the expert pool; it then carries that curve to a training set two and a half times the largest trial and names the all-labels configuration, whose forecast falls short of what such a run scores by more than its lead.
results: R1 the benchmark loss the largest map-transfer trial corresponds to; R2 what each tenth of a training set moved from expert to contractor or map-transfer labels adds to the benchmark loss; R3 the loss 512,000 expert labels would give; R4 each shortlisted configuration's expected benchmark loss; R5 the four-in-five range round the named one; R6 the configuration to name
one_fact_test: past the expert pool, take the level at each total as its own unknown, read off the vendor trials once each route's cost is taken out; rescues R3 and R6 (2 of 6): the forecasts past the pilot's largest trial and the range still have to be worked
notes: strategy other: a staged-pilot scale-up forecast in which no one family carries the pick (a yardstick carried to runs it never scored, a route's cost read at matched examples and learning rate, a return to more examples that bends past the range, chosen by holding out the largest runs); calibration organ: the pilot's benchmark submissions overlap the trainer's development scores on the same final checkpoints (two yardsticks over the same runs); context artifact: the group's meeting notes that carry the shortlist; overuse.objective answered in the design note
